paragraphs: David wanted to build God a house. It was a good heart, and Nathan even said, "Go and do all that is in your heart" (2 Samuel 7:3). But God flipped the whole thing around and said, "The LORD declares to you that He Himself will establish a house for you" (2 Samuel 7:11). Friend, David showed up with a cedar plan and God showed up with FOREVER.

Here's what that teaches me. We love to think God needs our work, but God is the one who gives first. He reminded David that He took him from the pasture, from following the flock, and made him ruler over Israel (2 Samuel 7:8). And He promised a descendant whose throne He would establish forever (2 Samuel 7:13). Whatever good thing you bring to God, He was already holding something bigger.

So look at how David answers. He sits before the LORD and says, "Who am I, O Lord GOD?" (2 Samuel 7:18). Then he turns the spotlight right onto God: "How great You are, O Lord GOD!" (2 Samuel 7:22). That's the way to take a gift, baker. You don't brag, you don't bargain, you just say thank You and ask Him to bless what He promised, because "You, O Lord GOD, have spoken" (2 Samuel 7:29).
